Workshop 4 · Practice problems

Good review or bad review?

Work these out by hand, without running code, the way the exam works. Total 24 marks. Fractions are fine as answers; a calculator helps only for turning them into percentages.

Print

Problems 1 to 3 are about a fake-review detector. In a shop, 20 of every 1000 reviews are fake. The detector flags 90% of fake reviews, and also wrongly flags 5% of genuine ones.

  1. [3]

    Count 1000 reviews. (a) How many fake reviews are flagged? (b) How many genuine reviews are flagged? (c) A review is flagged. What is the chance it really is fake?

  2. [2]

    In problem 1, give the value of the prior, the likelihood, the evidence and the posterior, each with a one-line meaning.

  3. [3]

    Now use the formulas, without counting reviews. (a) Work out P(flag) with the law of total probability. (b) Work out P(fake | flag) with Bayes' theorem. Check it against problem 1.

  4. [2]

    Start from the product rule, P(A ∩ B) = P(A | B) · P(B) = P(B | A) · P(A), and show in two steps how it gives Bayes' theorem.

  5. [2]

    Problems 5 to 8 use these six kettle reviews:

    positive:  it boils fast  ·  fast and quiet  ·  love it  ·  quiet kettle
negative:  it leaks       ·  slow and broke

    (a) What are the priors P(pos) and P(neg)? (b) How many words are in the positive pile and in the negative pile, and how many different words, V, do the six reviews use?

  6. [3]

    Without smoothing, work out (a) P(fast | pos) (b) P(it | neg) (c) P(leaks | pos). (d) What does (c) do to the positive score of any review containing leaks?

  7. [4]

    Use add-one smoothing, V = 10. Classify the review "quiet but slow". Show both scores, and give the chance it is positive.

  8. [3]

    (a) With add-one smoothing, classify "it leaks". (b) Work out the two scores again without the priors. What did the prior do?

  9. [2]

    Why is Naïve Bayes called naïve? Give a review where this goes wrong, and say what the classifier would do with it.

Answers will be released on the Workshop 4 page after class.
